chunks: Yunus narrated from Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in

a man who said to his wife, 'I have not come to you as a virgin (or: you have not remained a virgin),' he said, 'It is of no consequence, because the virginity (or: the hymen) goes away without sexual intercourse.'

key_terms.الْعُذْرَةُ: The hymen or the membrane of virginity.
key_terms.عَذْرَاءُ: A virgin woman, specifically referring to one whose hymen is intact.
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِشَيْءٍ: It is of no consequence / It does not matter (a legal phrase indicating the claim is weak or invalid).

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling if a husband claims his wife was not a virgin at the time of marriage?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that a husband's claim of non-virginity is legally inconsequential because the hymen (al-'udhrat) is not exclusive to sexual intercourse, as it can be lost through physical exertion or natural causes. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of caution in imposing penalties for defects, prioritizing the stability of the marriage contract over strict biological assumptions. It reflects the broader scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between physical signs and actual marital status in cases of khula' or annulment.
